TCA-RNG-CITRATE-PROCHIRALITY-01.claim: Citrate is prochiral; aconitase discriminates citrate's two carboxymethyl groups, so the two acetyl-CoA carbons don't become equivalent until after the first TCA turn.
TCA-RNG-CITRATE-PROCHIRALITY-01.source: LibreTexts: Jakubowski & Flatt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol. II, Ch 16 The Citric Acid Cycle (section 16.02) + Wikipedia 'Aconitase' (Mechanism) co-citations
TCA-RNG-CITRATE-PROCHIRALITY-01.claim_text: Citrate is a prochiral molecule; citrate synthase produces a specific stereoisomer, and aconitase discriminates between citrate's two carboxymethyl groups, so the two carbons derived from acetyl-CoA do not become equivalent until after the first turn of the cycle.
TCA-RNG-CITRATE-PROCHIRALITY-01.review_notes: Grounds the TCA RNG shuffle mechanism. Source updated from LEHNINGER-CH-CITRIC_ACID_CYCLE (rejected per user license concern 2026-08-15) to LIBRETEXTS-METAB-TCA (Jakubowski & Flatt, Fundamentals of Biochemistry Vol. II, Ch 16 The Citric Acid Cycle, section 16.02 'Reactions of the Citric Acid Cycle'). Source verified 2026-08-15 at https://bio.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Biochemistry/Fundamentals_of_Biochemistry_(Jakubowski_and_Flatt)/02%3A_Unit_II-_Bioenergetics_and_Metabolism/16%3A_The_Citric_Acid_Cycle/16.02%3A__Reactions_of_the_Citric_Acid_Cycle. The page covers: (1) citrate synthase stereospecificity - explicitly 'to form (S)-citryl CoA' then citrate (citrate synthase produces a specific stereoisomer); (2) the aconitase mechanism including the 180-degree flip of the cis-aconitate intermediate ('This cis-aconitate intermediate in the interconversion of citrate and isocitrate undergoes a 1800 flip around the C=C double bond'), which is the enzymatic discrimination between citrate's two carboxymethyl groups; (3) the cycle is presented 'in wedge/dash form with stereochemistry included'; (4) Krebs's isotope-labeling discovery using 14C-labeled intermediates. CAVEAT: the page does NOT explicitly use the word 'prochiral' for citrate (it uses 'prochiral' only for NADH) and does NOT explicitly state 'the two acetyl-CoA carbons do not become equivalent until after the first turn' - that consequence is the standard biochemistry implication of the stereospecific citrate synthase + aconitase discrimination mechanism the page DOES describe. The claim_text is faithful to the mechanism in the source. The RNG weight VALUES are a separate game-design claim (TCA-RNG-WEIGHT-01) approved individually. Approved by human 2026-08-15 (first batch, high-stakes individual review). 2026-09-01 batch-B D2(a): source set WIDENED with WIKIPEDIA-ACONITASE + WIKIPEDIA-TCA co-citations (Wikipedia 'Aconitase' Mechanism supplies verbatim the pro-R/pro-S prochirality wording + the OAA-vs-acetyl discrimination + the 180-degree citrate-mode-to-isocitrate-mode flip, fetched live 2026-08-30, rev 1343733503); claim text UNCHANGED; the human's batch-B 'All defaults' reply covers the widened set. Re-verified live 2026-08-30 (07-RESEARCH-tca-rng.md section 3): 16.02 text confirms (S)-citryl CoA + the 180-degree flip; the registered CAVEAT above remains accurate for 16.02 alone - the Wikipedia co-cite closes the 'prochiral' gap.
